reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate and partly cannot run. (1) Wrong baseline: the descended system is block-multihomogeneous (m blocks of l variables, degree 2^(m-1) per block), so MV < total-degree Bezout trivially. prediction_if_true ('MV/Bezout decays exponentially') is therefore not the right contrast. Analytic check (not yet run numerically): for m=2 with a dense F_p-linear base, supports are the box 2*Delta_l x 2*Delta_l and MV = C(2l,l)*4^l, which equals the multihomogeneous Bezout number and is ~16^l/sqrt(pi*l) against total-degree Bezout 16^l. The ratio is polynomial, so prediction_if_false is the expected outcome for any dense base. (2) The sparse/Hamming-ball/monomial-sparse base, which is the whole novelty, is absent from the toy. A Hamming ball is a union of C(n,w) coordinate subspaces, each with the same polytope as a dense subspace of dim w. Real sparsity can only come from a structured basis (normal basis with a sparse multiplication table) or a non-linear parametrisation, and the toy has no such arm. (3) No null arm: BKK is attained only for non-degenerate coefficients. Descended S_3 is known to be degenerate (Frobenius witness mu=x_R^-2 kills the degree-2 part, d_ff<=2), so msolve degree < MV is likely. 'msolve degree tracks MV' needs a control: random coefficients on the identical support. (4) Regime mismatch: MV is p-independent. p~2^10 with n<=5 is the Gaudry/Diem fixed-n large-p regime, where B*D^2<N is already known to hold. n=131 is p=2, where field equations enter, and the idea's own nongeneric argument says they restore full simplices. With field equations x^p-x on all N variables the square count is exactly p^N (brute force), a closed-form result needing no experiment. The toy therefore says nothing about n=131 as designed. (5) Feasibility: with n*m<=10 and n=3..5, m=2,3, the square cases (n=m*l) are only (n,m,l)=(2,2,1),(3,3,1),(4,2,2). There are no n-scaling data. csd/fpn_degrees.py descended_system('E') supports only n=2,3 (m=n, base x in F_p, symmetrised). S_5 has 54777 terms, so n=4,5 in that convention is not buildable within budget. It has no l>1 builder; one must be written. For non-square (n>m*l) the system is overdetermined and msolve returns [-1], so the degree is 0 and not comparable to MV. Also the BKK count is for the torus, so the affine version needs the origin added to every support. (6) Metric: MV, multihomogeneous Bezout and msolve ideal degree are structural counts and are fine; wall time is not used. But msolve ideal degree is not the solving degree (d_F), which is the wall actually named, so 'msolve degree tracks MV' does not touch the wall. Record the F4 max degree from 'msolve -v 2' as well.
fix: Redesign as a support-only, certificate-driven experiment with controls. STEP 0 (seconds, no msolve): compute exactly, for the descended S_{m+1} on a dense l-dim F_p-linear base, MV = N! * Vol(conv(support U {0})) when all supports are identical (else inclusion-exclusion of Minkowski-sum volumes via scipy.spatial.ConvexHull, N=m*l<=8), against (a) total-degree Bezout and (b) multihomogeneous Bezout; assert the closed form C(2l,l)*4^l for m=2. Run l=1..8 (m=2) and l=1..4 (m=3), i.e. n=m*l up to 16 and 12 on the support only, which gives a real n-trend. Use p=65521 and build components with an own l>1 builder (S_3 from csd.semaev.S3, S_4 for m=3, reduced mod p, tower field fd.GF(p,n)). Also run (n,m,l)=(2,2,1),(3,3,1) through fd.descended_system(E,xR,'E') as a cross-check. STEP 1 (the missing sparse arm): enumerate bases that could change supports, namely (i) random basis (control), (ii) normal basis / ONB type II, (iii) w-sparse coordinate subspaces, (iv) multiplicative-subgroup (mu_N) and trace-spectrum bases (lever 6). Report the support size and MV per basis. If all equal the dense case, the idea is closed with the theorem 'the polytope depends only on (m,l), not on the basis' (a relabelling kill of the sparse variant). STEP 2 (null arm): on square cases (4,2,2) and (2,2,1),(3,3,1), compare msolve ideal degree (msolve -g 2 -v 2, record the degree plus max F4 deg and the zero-reduction count) for (a) the real descended system, (b) random coefficients on the same support, and (c) MV. Predictions are pre-registered: true means real <= MV and MV/multihomogeneous Bezout decays like c^l with c<1; false means MV equals multihomogeneous Bezout up to poly(l), so the ratio to total Bezout is ~1/sqrt(l). STEP 3 (scaling certificate, the part that speaks to n=131): compute c_MV = log2(MV)/n against the non-genericity threshold from rule 5 with D>=MV, B=p^l, N=p^n: log2 MV < n*log2(p)*(m-1)/(2m). Evaluate at p=2 (the n=131 regime, where MV is p-independent), giving a threshold of about 0.25 bits per n at m=2 against c_MV~2 from the dense formula. State the verdict as the gap in exponent, extrapolated by the closed form. Add field equations only as the analytic arm (square count = p^N = brute force), with a p=2,3,5 check on n<=8 by msolve -g 2 if wanted. Cost: STEP 0-1 well under 2 CPU-min; STEP 2 under 5 CPU-min (sizes N<=4 variables, p=65521); total <10 CPU-min. Success metrics are integers (MV, Bezout numbers, ideal degree, F4 max degree), not wall time. Classification remains accounting unless STEP 1 finds a base with a strictly smaller polytope.
